about: Bowed before the middle of the altar, the priest says this prayer quietly. He asks the Holy Trinity to accept his service and sacrifice and, in mercy, to make it propitiatory for him and for all those for whom it was offered.

s01.narrative: Then the celebrant bows before the middle of the altar, joins his hands upon it, and says secretly:

s02.translation: May the homage of my service please Thee, O holy Trinity; and grant that the sacrifice which I, unworthy, have offered before the eyes of Thy majesty may be acceptable to Thee, and may win favour, through Thy mercy, for me and for all those for whom I have offered it. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.function: The subject is not the priest but “obséquium” (w005), the homage — that is what is to please God.

w004.function: Vocative. Here the prayer addresses the Trinity by name.

w007.function: Agrees with “servitútis” (w006) and marks the first person singular.

w012.function: Neuter, agreeing with “sacrifícium” (w011), and object of “óbtuli” (w017).

w013.function: Dative depending on “óbtuli” (w017). The phrase means “I offered before the eyes of Thy majesty.”

function_citations.title: Lewis and Short, A Latin Dictionary

w013.note: The form is dative and ablative plural at once. Nothing in the sentence decides whether the sacrifice is offered TO the eyes of Thy majesty or BEFORE them. This edition takes the dative and marks the doubt.

w016.function: Nominative: it describes the man who offers, not the offering — “I, unworthy, have offered”.

w020.function: Neuter, because what it says is said of “sacrifícium” (w011).

w021.function: Mihi with enclitic -que means “and for me”. The enclitic shifts the stress to the preceding syllable.

w029.function: With “miseránte” (w030) it forms an ablative absolute, which English turns into a clause: “Thou showing mercy”, that is, through Thy mercy.

w030.function: The present participle of deponent “miseror”, active in form.
